newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan labor reform changes add $300 mln.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan labor reform changes add $300 mln.

text.p: Modifications to Venezuela's crucial labor law reform made by the lower house of Congress last week will add some 150 billion bolivars ($300 million) to final costs, the Labor Minister said.
Venezuela previously estimated that the labor law reform, which forms part of a wider revamping of Venezuela's rigid labor markets, would cost around 540 billion bolivars ($1.1 billion).
The extra spending comes as the government faces growing criticism that it does not have the money to pay for a 70 percent public sector wage increase, granted in February.
"Apart from the additional cost, the government is also worried about Congress's delay in approving the reform," Labor Minister Maria Bernardoni told reporters.
The bill is due to be discussed by Congress's Upper Chamber, or Senate, on Wednesday.
